cells.quote: We found no signi ﬁcant effects (Table 5), suggesting age-related increases in IPS connectivity are speci ﬁcally related to math, but not reading, skills.
cells.note: The study reports no significant Word Reading association and provides no effect size, equivalence test, or adequate-power claim.

O.outcome_detail: Reported frequency of use

cells.quote: Among the included studies, CBD was the most frequently used type of learning activity, and participating in a collaborative activity was the most commonly used teaching strategy.
cells.note: Narrative scoping-review synthesis; no pooled effect size was reported.

O.outcome_detail: Reported frequency of teaching-strategy use

cells.quote: Participating in a collaborative activity was the most frequently reported strategy across the 41 studies.
cells.note: Narrative scoping-review synthesis; frequency was compared descriptively rather than through a statistical effect estimate.

D.comparison: Larger facilitator-to-student ratios or distracted facilitators

O.outcome_detail: Opportunities for interaction, timely feedback, guided discussion, and learner reception

cells.quote: These lower ratios were consistently associated with more opportunities for interaction, timely feedback, and guided discussion [16].
cells.note: The review reports an association across included studies, not a pooled causal estimate.

O.outcome_detail: Reflection and feedback on participants' learning experiences

cells.quote: Facilitator-led debriefing sessions in which feedback was given on the participants learning experiences were deemed essential [41].
cells.note: This is a narrative recommendation reported in the scoping review; the text does not provide a direct controlled comparison or effect size.
